subject: Incorporating handheld GPS accuracy and default DOP=1

messages.author: 721e86a05934645d
messages.subject: Incorporating handheld GPS accuracy and default DOP=1
parts:
Hi Chris,

I have been looking into using ctmm for VHF homing data.
I have two seasons of locations collected at inconsistent intervals with GPS accuracy ranging 1-7m.
Is there some way to incorporate GPS accuracy in lieu of DOP values? 
I ran my data through the code and it defaults DOP=1 for all points however, I lack experience working with DOP information and I am not sure if the default DOP=1 and output are appropriate to interpret.

Thank you!
Diana

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Incorporating handheld GPS accuracy and default DOP=1
parts:
Hi Diana,

If ctmm defaulted to DOP=1, then that means that as.telemetry couldn't find any error information in your data. Do you have time-specific error information on the location estimates, like a column of individual GPS accuracies?
If you don't, then you can assign a prior to the errors that ranges 1-7 meters, as detailed at the end of vignette('error') .

Best,
Chris

Hi Diana,

Okay, it's an error in meters of unknown proportionality. I'll add that column name to as.telemetry(). For the moment, you can import it as an HDOP column and then (preferably) collect some calibration data to fit the proportionality constant or (less preferably) assign a prior centered on 1.

https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.06.12.130195v2

https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/articles/error.html

Best,
Chris
